basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 21-22.' and it opens 'VERS. 21, 22.-- Non igitur ulra percutiam omnem animam, sicut feci cunctis diebus terrae.'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 21, 22.-- Non igitur ulra percutiam omnem animam, sicut feci cunctis diebus terrae. Sementis et messis, frigus et aestus, aestas et hiems, nox et dies non requiescent. Sementis et messis, id est doctrinae Scripturarum. | Per frigus et aestatem castitatem et fidem designat; per noctem et diem, Vetus et Novum Testamentum. Aliter, per sementem et messem doctores, et scripturas [ Petr. scriptores] haereseos ostendit [ Z., appellat]; per frigus et aestatem, infidelitatem et fidei claritatem; per noctem et diem haereses in utroque Testamento volunt intelligi.
